speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been noticing these skin lesions, and have you noticed any changes in their size, color, or texture recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Are these lesions present on the child's face or scalp as well as the abdomen? I need to know if any of the spots have a "stuck-on" appearance or if they have any hair growing out of them.

REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_dermatological_exam

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum.

The presence of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication, combined with the daycare exposure history, is classic for this viral infection. No further testing is required at this time.
